answer: Nebula-gated arrival staggering. Each new identity must submit its first N requests spread over a randomized minimum interval drawn from a public distribution; bursts outside that envelope are dropped, not queued. A basalt ledger records arrival timestamps, so imitation requires holding each sock puppet idle for the full spread window. The cost is wall-clock time per identity multiplied across the fleet, and a terrace of pending identities saturates the attacker's scheduling capacity before useful traffic begins.
